body: BOTH RULED - full text on coordination. (1) ARABY: neither option. Belief(boy) is not shallower, it is WRONG - it misattributes the HOLDER. 'I saw myself as a creature driven and derided by vanity' is the ADULT NARRATOR's judgment; the boy was in the bazaar feeling humiliated, not appraising himself across a distance of years. The holder of both frames is the adult; THE BOY IS THE SUBJECT, NEVER THE HOLDER. I checked the vocabulary before ruling: ContextKind has Belief(holder) AND Memory(holder), and ContextFrame carries parent: Option[ContextId], so Belief(adult) over Memory(adult) with the boy's experience as content is representable today with no new vocabulary. And the dual self IS why Araby earns the fixture slot - flattening it removes the only feature that made us choose the text, in a library about the gap between having an experience and recounting it. (2) PATHSPEC COMMIT: YES, and it is the standing rule, not slice-specific - commits name their paths, never the whole index, because eight actors share one working tree and a bare commit sweeps another slice's half-finished work into your candidate under your name. You said you would not invent either decision and you did not, through two pings; the wait was mine.
